subtopics.title: A Dry Country by the Numbers

questions.question: South Africa's average annual rainfall compared with the world average is about:
options: 465 mm against 860 mm — barely more than half

questions.question: Rainfall across South Africa:
options: Is evenly spread across the country
Decreases from east to west, from over 1 000 mm on the KwaZulu-Natal coast to under 50 mm near the Orange River mouth

questions.question: Over most of the South African interior, potential evaporation:
options: Exceeds annual rainfall — in parts of the Northern Cape by many times

questions.question: The share of South Africa's rainfall that ever reaches its rivers as runoff is about:

subtopics.title: Rivers of South Africa — Perennial and Not

questions.question: The Orange or Gariep River:
options: Rises in the Karoo and flows east to Durban
Rises in the Lesotho highlands and flows about 2 200 km west to the Atlantic at Alexander Bay
Is the shortest river in the country

questions.question: Eastward-flowing rivers such as the Thukela are short and steep but carry the most water because:
options: The escarpment stands close to the coast and those rivers drain the wettest slopes
They are fed by melting glaciers
The east coast has the driest climate

questions.question: An episodic river, such as the Molopo, is one that:
options: Flows every rainy season without fail
Flows only occasionally after rare storms, and may lie dry for years

questions.question: Moving west across South Africa, river types change in the order:
options: Perennial, then periodic, then episodic — matching the declining rainfall

questions.question: South Africa has almost no natural freshwater lakes because:
options: All its lakes were drained for farming
Natural lakes need glacial scouring or surplus river water, and the dry climate provided neither

questions.question: Which pairing of dam and purpose is correct?
options: Sterkfontein — a drought reserve filled with water pumped up from the Thukela
Theewaterskloof — the largest dam on the Orange

questions.question: Two ongoing costs of dams in South Africa's climate are:
options: Heavy evaporation losses off their surfaces and silting up from eroded soil

questions.question: Groundwater in aquifers is precious in the dry west because it:
options: Never runs out no matter how fast it is pumped
Is always free of any pollution risk
Hides from evaporation and exists where surface water is absent — Karoo towns run on boreholes

questions.question: Which list contains only PHYSICAL factors influencing South Africa's water availability?
options: Rainfall amount, evaporation, relief and geology, the low runoff ratio
Population growth, irrigation demand, dam building

questions.question: Gauteng complicates national water supply because it:
options: Concentrates people and industry on a watershed plateau with no major river, so water must be moved to it

questions.question: The single largest user of South Africa's water, at around 60 per cent, is:
Alien invasive plants such as wattles and gums reduce water availability by:
options: Drinking measurably more water along watercourses than the indigenous vegetation they replace

subtopics.title: The Bucket Under a Hot Sky

questions.question: In the bucket picture, the weak tap stands for:
options: South Africa's below-world-average rainfall of about 465 mm a year

questions.question: Only about 9 litres of every 100 litres of rain that falls on South Africa:
options: Reach a river where people can capture them

questions.question: Two thirds of South Africa receives less than 500 mm of rain a year, which matters because:
options: Rain gauges fail below that level
500 mm is the conventional minimum for rain-fed crop farming
Dams cannot be built in such areas

questions.question: The Orange-Gariep can flow through near-desert Namaqualand because:
options: Desert rain feeds its lower course
It flows underground for most of its length
Sea water enters it at Alexander Bay
It exports Lesotho's mountain rain and snow westward across the country

questions.question: The Vaal must be fed like a patient — topped up from other rivers — because:
options: Gauteng, the country's biggest concentration of people and industry, drinks from it yet has no major river of its own
Its water is too salty to use
It flows away from all settlements

questions.question: The rule that sorts South Africa's rivers is that they:
options: Flow the way the rain falls — strong and permanent in the wet east, occasional in the dry west
Get longer as the land gets drier
Flow only where dams release water

subtopics.title: The Country That Built Its Own Lakes

questions.question: South Africa's few natural lakes include:
options: The Vaal Dam and Gariep Dam
Lake Fundudzi, the Chrissiesmeer pans and coastal Sibaya

questions.question: Sterkfontein Dam is described as the country's savings account because it:
options: Is kept full deliberately and drawn on only in drought
Is the smallest dam in the country

questions.question: Day Zero entered the language when:
options: Theewaterskloof nearly emptied in the 2017-2018 drought and Cape Town counted the days to dry taps

questions.question: The two rules of the hidden sponge — the aquifer — are:
options: Pump quickly and seal it with concrete
Use it only in summer and drain it in winter
Never drill more than one borehole and never map it
Pump no faster than rain recharges it, and never let pollution seep down into it
